summary: Proceed as a user-requested, below-bar judge check. Fresh (blob 315119e2 = mint blob, BEST 1.6904 unchanged); CLAIMS:98's >= 2.5% reopen is waived by the user steer. A +1.31% headline cannot be read in one run (board CI is about +-1.5%, the margin is 1.24%, rows drift 1.5-2.5%). The build must make its own readout: pinned or pair-gated routes, ROUTE lines, distinct kernel names, a DQ0 control instantiation, and an in-prepare master-vs-wh layer A/B on the real ea4x fork at T=128 and T=256. With those, no companion check is needed.
justification: A. The mechanism is plausible and measured. The 7cc034f9 profile has the wgmma hot half at 153.5 us (wg<true> 102.1 + wg<false> 51.4) on verify_32 sliding, 130.6 on verify_32 full and 69.6 on verify_16 sliding, against a ~39 us T=256 floor (LOG 1749Z; hothalf-1029 sec. 2: K-step x1.36-4 over the padded-N tensor floor, 576 token columns for 386 routes). All three parts attack measured gaps: (1) the serial dequant chain (A3, 287 -> 223 warp-inst/stage); (2) padding (nx, N80 1294 -> 1063 cyc/stage); (3) MMA exposure at N >= 48 (ring, N128 1296 -> ~1115-1170). These are per-SM cycle effects on a consumer-bound kernel, the class that transfers to the H200, and the prefill A3 transfer (node 0.84-0.89 vs judge 0.854/0.909) confirms that path. Expected shapes and directions match TASK's rows: only verify_16/32 (T=128/256) run the hybrid, and decode_* / verify_1 stay flat. WEAKEST LINK: the forked end-to-end ratio. The node used a spin stand-in for ea4x, with no ALU/L2 contention, calibrated to R=1.97 at T=128. The judge profile shows a much heavier cold side at verify_16 sliding: ea4x w13+w2 197 us vs hot 69.6 under concurrency. So the T=128 share of the estimate (D128 -10.4 us = ~0.48 of the 1.31 points) may hide behind the cold half, leaving ~+0.8% from T=256 alone. Second weakest: exact-N's 8 instantiations cost 2-6% at unchanged N (code size). On a judge draw with mostly N64/N128 chunks, nx alone could be neutral; the per-draw gain is very draw-dependent (verify_32 sliding vs full hot pair 153.5 vs 130.6 us on the board). Prior: the frontmatter says 'prior: none' but the body names S1a (CLAIMS:72). The true closest priors are CLAIMS:98 (A3 alone, this stack's parent lead), CLAIMS:59 (wg2 re-split, refuted) and the old wait<1>/ping-pong D4-varB, which ptxas serialized (C7512). The difference is real: the hh2 SASS shows DEPBAR.LE 0x1/0x2 per k16, not serialized, and the ring is limited to N >= 48, where it measured gains. This is a clerical defect, not grounds for hold. Fix the field to name CLAIMS:98/59. Nothing on FINDINGS' Do-not-try list matches.
confounders: v4xd-stack (CLAIMS:95, the board, master d28b23d7): owns the priority-0 fork stream and the T=128 cold half v4cxs. The hot-half cut's end-to-end value is set by this fork's residency order: 2 x 113 KB ea4x CTAs/SM exclude a 187/204 KB wg CTA. A flat T=128 row could be the fork hiding a real kernel gain, not a non-transfer. Answered in-run by the forked layer A/B (see interference). No revert needed: the fork is only x1.013-1.026 over serial.

pinned trim (CLAIMS:69) H-16 at T=128/256: fixes the hot set (> 16 routes, block 16) and so the N distribution exact-N sees. Retuning H would change both the hot set and nx's value. Keep it pinned and unchanged so the A/B stays clean.

W6-G fast silu in wg (CLAIMS:68) and W6-B diet cells (CLAIMS:64): they share the wg epilogue and the T>=128 launch sequence. Exact-N changes the epilogue's NB loop bounds (NB/8 must stay even, true for 48/80/96/112). Outputs must stay bit-identical, so the build's torch.equal check covers the interaction.
Engine A L3/L4 (CLAIMS:74/78): the same dq2 paired-scale form, already in decode for the cold half. Same numerics family; it does not confound timing, because the cold half's code is unchanged.
v4x port (CLAIMS:93): the T=128 cold half is v4cxs. Its runtime sets how much of the T=128 hot cut can surface. See fork above.
interference: C. No companion check. Every ambiguity is cheaper to resolve inside the same run, and a revert or tune companion would not sharpen a +1.3% headline: one run's noise (~1.5% CI, 1.5-2.5% row drift) swamps it either way. What makes a single result interpretable, and what the build MUST include: (1) ROUTE certainty. CLAIMS:69 found that prepare-time layer margins do not track judged rows, and the T=128 layer cut is ~10 us of ~334 (x0.97, right at the proposed 0.98 bar), so a forked-layer race would flip. Route on the ISOLATED hot pair (w13 -> PDL w2 graph, read-flushed, interleaved), where wh reads x0.82-0.90. Require <= 0.97 vs master's dispatched launch AND vs an in-module DQ0 control, every round (prefill's REGA_DQ rule), plus bit-exactness. Otherwise pin wh, given exactness. Print [hh-wh] ROUTE T=128/T=256 with the per-round ratios. (2) PROOF IN THE PROFILE. Give the new kernels a distinct name or template argument (e.g. wg_kernel<G,1>), so the okc profile shows per row which hot half ran and its GPU time. The readable signal is the verify_32 sliding hot pair: 153.5 us on the board, ~126-131 predicted for wh, ~139-141 for A3 alone. That is a ~15-20% kernel-level move, far above drift, unlike the headline. (3) THE FORK ANSWER the node could not give. After routing, at T=128 and T=256 time a 2 x 2 layer-level arm set {master hot, wh hot} x {serial, fork} on the real ea4x cold half: interleaved, read-flushed, >= 2 inputs x 2 rounds as _sfk_gate does. Print it as [hh-wh] FORK lines. That alone decides whether a flat verify_16 row is 'the fork hid it' or 'no transfer'. (4) A DQ0 control instantiation in the new module: master's dq_stage, buckets and ring text compiled in the new TU. It separates the module/codegen effect from each part. Report fidelity DQ0 / master within 0.97-1.03, else mark INVALID and keep master. Optionally add a3-only and a3+nx pair arms (prepare-only timing, not routed) to attribute the 1.31% among the parts. Decision rule for the readout: a scored run only if the check headline beats 1.6904 by the 1.24% margin. If wh routed in both classes, the profile hot pair is <= x0.90 at verify_32 and the rows are flat or noisy, record [shelf] with the kernel/row numbers and carry wh as a bit-exact rider on the next decode candidate (as the forkguard rode). Kill if the profile hot pair at verify_32 sliding is > ~140 us (A3-only level), or if a route reads OFF. Use the row-level 416 us rule only as a secondary check: it sits inside verify_32 sliding's ~6-11 us run drift.
rules_flags: Data-derived caching risk. The hypothesis says 'a prepare-time word-permuted copy of the HOT experts' code bank', but which experts are hot depends on the input. Permute the whole wg bank (all LOCAL_EXPERTS; wg_banks is already a separate copy, so in-place is fine once master's arm is no longer needed) from weights only, never from a sample routing.

A3 exactness precondition: every scale byte in [0x08, 0x7E] (positive normal e4m3). Scan the whole wg bank in prepare (as prefill's REGA_DQ_SCALE_LO/HI does). On any miss, keep master's hot half. Final review reruns held-out data and nearby shapes, so this must not be assumed from today's weights.

Exact-N selection must stay device-side: a switch on the chunk's nbk inside the kernel, with all 8 tensor maps encoded per call over the scratch buffer as today's 4 are. No host branching on route counts (that would need a sync / value-dependent control flow in the graph).

Ring hazard: the R=4 A-register ring with wait<2> is safe only if a ring slot is rewritten >= 3 commits after its group, and each smem stage is released only after every wgmma reading its B slab has retired. A premature release is a timing-dependent race that a single canary can miss, and judge timing (real fork contention) differs from the node's. Run the exactness check over many replays on both states (like the existing 16-replay [hotcold] copy check), not one launch.

Build log: grep the load_inline/ptxas output for C75xx (wgmma serialization) and print regs/spill per new kernel. A serialized ring is still exact but would silently turn the ring part into a loss. Do not spawn cuobjdump (process start is a rule flag); use the compiler output already captured and cudaFuncGetAttributes.

Size cap: decode is 955,413 B, about 44.6 KB below 1,000,000 B. The new dq text + 8 generated Wg<NB> specializations + ring loop + race/diag code must fit after build.py's comment strip (which triggers at > 990 KB). Measure before dispatch; trim dead diag text first if needed.

Prepare budget: the board's prepare reaches ~125 s (W6P summary 124.4 s) of the 300 s limit, and _sfk_gate's deadline is 250 s. A separate module (~35-40 s nvcc on the judge) must start in a background thread at the top of prepare and be joined before prepare returns (prefill idiom). All wh steps need their own deadline guard (e.g. no step after ~240 s), falling back to master.
Log tail: the board's log is already 14,044 B of the 16,000-char tail. Keep the [hh-wh] summary <= ~1.5 KB, or trim other prints, so the [hotcold] anatomy and [w6m-fork] lines are not pushed out.
freshness: E. Fresh: BEST 1.6904 (7cc034f9) = best_at_mint; master's submission.py blob = 315119e2 = mint_blob; 0.00% movement against the 1.24% margin. CLAIMS:98 [lead] (A3 in the hot half) is the newest claim for this mechanism. Its reopen ('stack with a w2 wave/tail fix and per-expert N-tile fix to >= 2.5%; judge check of the stack') is only partly met: the N-tile fix is in, the w2 split was killed in hh2 sec. 3 and the ring replaces it, and the estimate is 1.31% < 2.5%. The user steer of 10-29 ~15:04Z ('run all you want that youre able to', below-bar user-requested runs allowed; H100-derived work first) and user_requested: true cover this. Not a hold. Checked and not blocking: CLAIMS:72 S1a refuted (a different kernel; this keeps wg_kernel); CLAIMS:59 wg2 refuted (re-split, not dequant/N/ring); CLAIMS:67 fork refuted on 10-27 but superseded in practice by the landed fork in CLAIMS:94-95, which this keeps unchanged; CLAIMS:69 / CLAIMS:95 own the rows as the base this builds on, not with a competing mechanism. No [superseded] or [refuted] claim owns A3 / exact-N / ring in the hot half.
open_questions: Which judge us does the T=128 hot cut buy under the real ea4x fork? The profile's cold/hot at verify_16 sliding is ~2.8x, against the stand-in's calibrated 1.97x. If ~0, the expected headline is ~+0.8%, not +1.31%.

Does nx's code-size tax (2-6% at unchanged N) show on the judge's actual T=256 draws? Board verify_32 sliding vs full differ by 23 us in the hot pair, so N mixes differ per row. A prepare-time a3 vs a3+nx pair arm would answer it.
Should the moe twin get A3 alone in the same session? hh2 says moe gains ~+0.9% from A3 and nothing from nx or the ring. Keep this decode check decode-only, so its readout is not entangled.
Should master's unpermuted wg bank be freed after routing (memory ~0.9 GB), or kept for a per-class split route (T=128 master, T=256 wh)? The build must keep it if the routes can differ per class.
